title: 11D Projection Upgrade — Task Sufficiency, Fiber Ambiguity and Reconstruction Bounds
status: archive-generated mathematical contribution extending the recovered 11D projection architecture; information theory and metric-space results, not evidence for physical 11-dimensional spacetime
abstract: The strongest rigorous form of the 11D projection programme is an inverse-problem theory of what survives reduction. This upgrade replaces the vague candidate invariant I*(M_d)=I*(M_(d±1)) with three precise questions: whether the original state is reconstructible, whether a chosen task-relevant variable is preserved, and how ambiguity grows along a chain of projections. A projection may destroy microscopic information while remaining perfectly sufficient for a declared task. Conversely, a visually or symbolically compelling lower-dimensional image may be unable to determine its higher-dimensional source because an entire fiber of distinct states shares the same projection. The new formulation supplies an exact fiber-ambiguity lower bound, a task-sufficiency criterion in conditional mutual information, a data-processing rule for dimensional descent, and a reconstruction-defect measure for proposed lifting operators.

setup.state: X in P, where P may be an 11D physical configuration space, a high-dimensional state space, or another explicitly declared measurable/metric space
setup.task_variable: Z is a declared target quantity whose prediction/inference matters
setup.rule: Physical compactification, statistical compression and generic projection remain distinct interpretations even when they use the same mathematics.

result_1_fiber_ambiguity_bound.statement: For any metric d on P, any projection pi, any y, and any deterministic decoder R, sup_{x in F_y} d(x,R(y)) >= (1/2) diam(F_y), where diam(F_y)=sup_{x1,x2 in F_y} d(x1,x2).
result_1_fiber_ambiguity_bound.proof_sketch: Choose x1,x2 in the fiber whose separation approaches diam(F_y). Since both project to the same y, the decoder returns the same R(y). By the triangle inequality d(x1,x2) <= d(x1,R(y))+d(R(y),x2), so at least one reconstruction error is at least half their separation. Taking the supremum gives the bound.
result_1_fiber_ambiguity_bound.meaning: A broad fiber creates irreducible worst-case ambiguity. No clever lifting operator can recover which member of the fiber was original without extra side information, priors or measurements.
result_1_fiber_ambiguity_bound.project_contribution: This gives the project's hidden-dimension/fiber language a hard quantitative limit: hidden multiplicity is not free reconstructible information.

result_2_task_sufficiency.statement: For deterministic Y=pi(X), the reduced representation Y preserves all information in X relevant to a target Z exactly when I(Z;X|Y)=0. Equivalently, p(z|x)=p(z|y) almost surely and I(Z;Y)=I(Z;X) under the usual regularity assumptions.
result_2_task_sufficiency.interpretation: A projection can be globally lossy but task-lossless. The lower-dimensional description does not need to reconstruct every microscopic coordinate if the discarded coordinates contain no additional information about the declared target.
result_2_task_sufficiency.example_logic: A compactified/effective description might be sufficient for a low-energy observable even though it cannot reconstruct the microscopic high-dimensional state.
result_2_task_sufficiency.replacement_for_I_star: Instead of demanding a universal I* invariant, define a target-specific information retention Delta_task=I(Z;X)-I(Z;Y)>=0. Exact task sufficiency means Delta_task=0.

result_3_data_processing_descent.chain: X -> Y_10 -> Y_9 -> ... -> Y_4, with each Y_(d-1) obtained only from Y_d
result_3_data_processing_descent.rule: For any target Z connected through the same processing chain, I(Z;Y_(d-1)) <= I(Z;Y_d). Pure coarse-graining cannot create information about Z that was absent at the previous layer.
result_3_data_processing_descent.consequence: If a lower-dimensional stage appears more informative, the model must identify the added side information, prior, intervention or measurement rather than calling the increase spontaneous dimensional information gain.
result_3_data_processing_descent.dimension_ladder_metric: Define L_d(Z)=I(Z;Y_d)-I(Z;Y_(d-1))>=0 as task-information loss at one descent step. A proposed effective ladder is good for target Z when each L_d is acceptably small or when losses are explicitly understood.

result_4_reconstruction_risk.definition: D*=inf_R E[d(X,R(pi(X)))] over the declared decoder class.
result_4_reconstruction_risk.meaning: D* is the irreducible reconstruction distortion for the chosen metric, distribution and decoder class.
result_4_reconstruction_risk.zero_distortion_case: D*=0 only when X is recoverable from Y almost surely within the declared model class; in a deterministic exact setting this means the relevant states are effectively injectively represented by pi.
result_4_reconstruction_risk.rate_distortion_connection: If the representation itself is capacity-limited or stochastic, rate-distortion theory supplies the natural tradeoff between representation rate and tolerated reconstruction distortion.

result_5_section_is_not_inverse.right_inverse_condition: pi(R(y))=y says R is a section/right inverse on M.
result_5_section_is_not_inverse.missing_condition: It does not imply R(pi(x))=x for every x in P.
result_5_section_is_not_inverse.reconstruction_defect: epsilon_rec=E[d(X,R(pi(X)))] or a worst-case version quantifies the failure of R o pi to be the identity.
result_5_section_is_not_inverse.commuting_diagram_rule: Every claimed raise/lower cycle should report both the projection consistency defect d_M(pi(R(y)),y) and the source reconstruction defect d_P(R(pi(x)),x).

approximate_dimensional_invariant.proposal: Replace one universal invariant with a vector Q_d=(Delta_task,D_rec,T_top,C_sym), where Delta_task is target-information loss, D_rec is reconstruction distortion, T_top records selected topological invariants and C_sym records explicitly preserved symmetry data.
approximate_dimensional_invariant.reason: Different reductions preserve different kinds of structure. A scalar invariant hides whether preservation is informational, geometric, topological or dynamical.
approximate_dimensional_invariant.advancement_rule: Call a projection structurally faithful only relative to a declared tolerance vector and target, not because several unrelated quantities were rhetorically grouped as information.

minimal_experiments: Construct a synthetic 11D or high-dimensional state distribution with a known target Z and compare several projections pi_d by Delta_task and D_rec.
Demonstrate a case where exact state reconstruction fails because fibers are broad while task prediction remains lossless.
Demonstrate the opposite case where geometrically small reconstruction error still destroys a rare but task-critical variable.
For a physical compactification, identify the low-energy target observables first and test whether the effective variables form an approximately sufficient statistic for those observables.
failure_conditions: A proposed universal information invariant changes when the target variable or prior distribution changes and therefore was not universal.
The reconstruction decoder appears accurate only because the test distribution excludes large parts of the admissible fiber.
A lower-dimensional representation is called lossless even though I(Z;X|Y) is materially nonzero for the claimed target.
A physical dimensional-reduction claim never specifies which effective observables the reduced theory must preserve.

external_references.use: Established framework for compressing X while retaining information relevant to a target Y.
Example of using information theory and rate-distortion ideas to derive limits on reconstruction from projections.
Modern discussion linking informative summaries, approximate sufficiency and information-theoretic objectives.
